title: Commonwealth Games 2026: India's Complete Schedule, Medal Hopes and How to Watch From Abroad
excerpt: India sends a 126-member squad to Glasgow with Neeraj Chopra, Mirabai Chanu and Lovlina Borgohain leading the charge across 10 sports from July 23 to August 2.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India's 126-member squad competes in 10 sports at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games from July 23 to August 2.
  • Neeraj Chopra, Mirabai Chanu, and Lovlina Borgohain are key medal contenders for India.
  • Hockey, badminton, and table tennis are excluded, limiting India's traditional medal opportunities.
  • Live coverage available on Sony Sports Network, Doordarshan Sports, and Sony LIV streaming.
  • The para-sport contingent is India's largest ever at the Commonwealth Games, with 28 athletes.

A Leaner Games, Higher Stakes

The 2026 Commonwealth Games open in Glasgow on Thursday, July 23, with India fielding a 126-member contingent — the country's largest squad for an edition that features just 10 sports. The scaled-down programme, designed to cut hosting costs, has eliminated several disciplines where India historically dominates: hockey, badminton, table tennis and squash are all absent.

> **"Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu will carry the Indian flag at the opening ceremony.

"Our qualifying standards were not high; they were right."**

India's Medal Contenders
›Neeraj Chopra: Javelin, competing on July 30-31.
›Mirabai Chanu: Weightlifting, competing on July 26.
›Lovlina Borgohain: Boxing, competing from July 24 to August 1.
›Emerging talents: Murali Sreeshankar, Praveen Chithravel, and Tulika Maan.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=wr2c7806MuQ

That makes every available medal event count. The Sports Ministry approved a 191-member Indian contingent, comprising 126 athletes and 51 team officials. Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu will carry the Indian flag at the opening ceremony.

"Our qualifying standards were not high; they were right. There was a lot of science. We were criticised, but 32 people have qualified."

— Adille Sumariwalla, AFI Vice-President

India's Big Three

Javelin star Neeraj Chopra returns to competitive action after a back injury kept him off the circuit since the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo. He is scheduled to compete in qualifying on July 30 and the final on July 31 at Scotstoun Stadium. His biggest threat comes from Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem, the reigning Olympic champion.

In weightlifting, Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu is the clear favourite in the women's 48kg category on July 26. Bindyarani Devi and Gyaneshwari Yadav add depth to a squad expected to collect multiple medals.

Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain leads a 14-strong boxing contingent, with world champion Jaismine Lamboria and Preeti Pawar also in contention for gold. Boxing preliminary bouts begin on Day 2 (July 24), with finals on August 1.

![Mirabai Chanu. Neeraj Chopra, Mirabai Chanu, and Lovlina Borgohain are key medal contenders for India.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b9/Saikhom_Mirabai_Chanu.jpg)

Key Schedule Highlights (All Times IST)

July 23 (Day 1): Lawn Bowls group stage begins at 2:00 PM IST; Opening Ceremony at 10:30 PM IST.

July 26 (Day 4): Weightlifting finals — Men's 60kg (2:00 PM), Women's 48kg featuring Mirabai Chanu (6:30 PM), Men's 65kg (11:00 PM).

July 27 (Day 5): Athletics begins — 400m Hurdles, Long Jump and 110m Hurdles rounds from 2:30 PM; High Jump Final at 11:00 PM.

July 30 (Day 8): Men's Javelin Qualifying with Neeraj Chopra at 2:30 PM; Triple Jump Qualifying; Decathlon events.

July 31 (Day 9): Men's Javelin Final at 11:00 PM; Boxing Semi-finals from 3:00 PM.

August 1 (Day 10): Boxing Gold Medal Finals; Triple Jump Final; Men's 400m Final.

August 2 (Day 11): Judo heavyweight medals; Track Cycling finals; Closing Ceremony at 10:30 PM IST.

![Lovlina Borgohain. Neeraj Chopra, Mirabai Chanu, and Lovlina Borgohain are key medal contenders for India.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/82/Lovlina_Borgohain_in_August_2022.jpg)

Beyond the Medal Favourites

Long jumper Murali Sreeshankar, triple jumper Praveen Chithravel and distance runner Gulveer Singh represent India's emerging athletics talent. In judo, Tulika Maan in the heavyweight division is a strong medal contender. India's Lawn Bowls squad, which earned gold and silver in Birmingham 2022, opens India's campaign on Day 1.

The para-sport contingent is the largest India has ever sent to a CWG — 28 athletes across five disciplines. Soman Rana in Para-Athletics is among the leading medal hopes.

How to Watch

The Commonwealth Games 2026 will be broadcast on Sony Sports Network and Doordarshan Sports, with DD Free Dish carrying the signal. Live streaming is available on Sony LIV. Competitions are spread across four venues: the OVO Hydro (Opening Ceremony, Netball), Tollcross International Swimming Centre, Scotstoun Stadium (Athletics) and the Scottish Event Campus (Boxing, Judo, Weightlifting, Bowls).

For fans in the Indian diaspora, most medal events fall in the late evening IST window, which aligns with afternoon viewing in the UK and early morning on the US East Coast.

Key Schedule Highlights
July 23
Lawn Bowls group stage begins; Opening Ceremony at 10:30 PM IST.
July 26
Weightlifting finals, including Mirabai Chanu at 6:30 PM IST.
July 30
Men's Javelin Qualifying with Neeraj Chopra at 2:30 PM IST.
August 1
Boxing Gold Medal Finals and Men's 400m Final.
August 2
Closing Ceremony at 10:30 PM IST.
